prompt: What answers the Azure CLI in this course's lab when a command needs Azure Resource Manager?
hint: The lab has no imitation of Azure running.

choices.text: A local emulator of Resource Manager, started in a second terminal
choices.why: No such program exists for Resource Manager, and the course refuses to fake one.

choices.text: A free Azure subscription the platform lends each student
choices.why: The platform lends no account and no machine. The lab is yours, and has no account in it.

choices.text: Nothing: the CLI refuses before sending, because nobody signed in
choices.why: Right. `Please run 'az login'` comes from the CLI's own memory, with no request sent.

choices.text: Microsoft Entra ID, which answers for Resource Manager
choices.why: Entra ID answers sign-in requests, and refuses a made-up tenant. It never answers for Resource Manager.

prompt: A Bicep file compiles without an error. Which of these has it established?
hint: Three things only Azure can say stay unsaid.

choices.text: That the account deploying it has permission to
choices.why: Permission is judged by Resource Manager when the request arrives, and no request was sent.

choices.text: That every name in it is still free in Azure
choices.why: Whether somebody else took a name is a fact about Azure today, which a compiler cannot see.

choices.text: What the resources in it will cost per month
choices.why: No price is in a template. Prices come from Microsoft's price list, which the lesson's program reads.

choices.text: That its shape is one Resource Manager would accept
choices.why: Right. Types, names of properties and structure are checked; values that only Azure can judge are not.

prompt: Which of the three ways to get a terminal does the lesson recommend for somebody on Windows?
hint: One of them runs a real Ubuntu beside Windows.

choices.text: Installed, with Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL
choices.why: Right. `wsl --install -d Ubuntu-24.04` gives a real Ubuntu, and installed is the recommended path.

choices.text: Azure Cloud Shell, which has `az` already installed
choices.why: Cloud Shell needs an Azure account, and the course is built so that you never need one.

choices.text: A virtual machine in Hyper-V, since WSL is not real Linux
choices.why: WSL runs a real Ubuntu. The virtual machine is the path for a Mac, or for a computer you would rather not touch.

choices.text: Online, in a rented shell
choices.why: It works, but it is not the recommendation: it puts the lab on somebody else's terms and hours.

prompt: Why does this lab need one terminal, when a lab for a cloud with an emulator needs two?
hint: What would the second one be running?

choices.text: Because the Azure CLI starts its own server in the background
choices.why: The CLI starts when you type it and stops when it has answered. Nothing stays running.

choices.text: Because nothing here imitates Azure
choices.why: Right. Every tool starts on demand and stops when it has answered.

choices.text: Because Terraform and the CLI share one process
choices.why: They are separate programs. Neither runs in the background.

choices.text: Because WSL allows only one terminal at a time
choices.why: WSL opens as many terminals as you like. The count comes from the lab, not the system.

prompt: What does `AZURE_CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/azure/.azure"` in `env.sh` do?
hint: What does the CLI store?

choices.text: It tells the CLI which subscription to use
choices.why: A subscription is chosen after signing in. This variable says where the CLI keeps its files.

choices.text: It installs the CLI's extensions into that directory
choices.why: Extensions do land under it, but the point is everything the CLI stores, sign-ins included.

choices.text: It keeps the CLI's files, sign-ins included, in the lab
choices.why: Right. A terminal without it uses `~/.azure`, a CLI with a separate memory.

choices.text: It points every request at a local copy of Azure
choices.why: There is no local copy of Azure. Nothing in `env.sh` redirects a request.

prompt: Ubuntu ships Python without the package `python3-___`, which makes virtual environments.
hint: The module is called with `python3 -m`.

prompt: The lab's `du` printed 709M for the CLI's virtual environment, 117M for `~/azure/.azure` and 124M for Terraform. How many megabytes is that in all?
hint: Add the three.

prompt: Why does the course install the Azure CLI from the Python Package Index rather than Microsoft's `apt` repository?
hint: Look at what the block pins, and where.

choices.text: It pins one version in a directory of your own, without `sudo`
choices.why: Right. Microsoft puts `apt` first in its documentation; the index is the one that fits a pinned, removable lab.

choices.text: The `apt` package lacks the Bicep command
choices.why: Both install the same program, `az bicep` included.

choices.text: The package index has a newer CLI than the `apt` one
choices.why: Both carry the same releases. The difference is where it goes and who installs it.

choices.text: Microsoft no longer publishes an `apt` package for Ubuntu 24.04
choices.why: It does publish one. The lesson names it as the route Microsoft's documentation puts first.

prompt: A new terminal answers `az: command not found`, though the setup finished. What is the cure?
hint: What does a new terminal not have?

choices.text: Install `azure-cli` with `apt`, as Ubuntu suggests
choices.why: That installs a second CLI, outside the lab. The pinned one is already in `~/azure/venv`.

choices.text: Run `az login`, which sets up the path
choices.why: `az login` needs `az` to be found first, and signs you in to an account the course never uses.

choices.text: Run the `pip install` line again
choices.why: The CLI is installed. This terminal simply has not been pointed at it.

choices.text: Run `source ~/azure/env.sh` in that terminal
choices.why: Right. It enters the virtual environment, which is where `az` is.

prompt: `terraform version` answers *cannot execute binary file: Exec format error*. What went wrong?
hint: `uname -m` answers the question.

choices.text: The file was not made executable
choices.why: That gives *Permission denied*. This message says the shell read the file and could not run it at all.

choices.text: The zip was the build for another processor
choices.why: Right. `x86_64` takes `amd64`, `aarch64` takes `arm64`.

choices.text: Terraform needs a newer glibc than Ubuntu 24.04 has
choices.why: Terraform is one static program and needs no library from the system.

choices.text: The download was cut short and the file is damaged
choices.why: A truncated zip fails at `unzip`, before there is a program to run.

prompt: `az group list` answers `Please run 'az login' to setup account.` in the lab. What does that tell you?
hint: Did a request leave the computer?

choices.text: Resource Manager refused the request for lack of a token
choices.why: No request reached Resource Manager. The CLI stopped before sending one.

choices.text: The lab works: the CLI found no sign-in and sent nothing
choices.why: Right. Refusing without an account is the normal state of this lab.

choices.text: The Bicep CLI is missing and must be installed first
choices.why: Listing resource groups has nothing to do with Bicep.

choices.text: `AZURE_DEFAULTS_LOCATION` is not set in this terminal
choices.why: A default location fills in a missing parameter; it signs nobody in.

prompt: A classmate runs `az login` in the lab's terminal to stop the sign-in message, and signs in to their company's tenant. What is the risk the lesson names?
hint: Which CLI is now signed in?

choices.text: Their company is billed for every `az bicep build` they run
choices.why: Compiling sends nothing to Azure and costs nothing, signed in or not.

choices.text: The lab's Terraform stops working until they sign out
choices.why: Terraform's `validate` is unaffected by a sign-in.

choices.text: Microsoft disables the account for signing in from WSL
choices.why: Nothing prevents signing in from WSL. The danger is which terminal holds the sign-in.

choices.text: The next command copied from a lesson runs against a real subscription
choices.why: Right. The lab's memory now holds a real identity, which is why a real account belongs in a separate terminal.

prompt: Put the first hour of a new Azure account in the order the lesson gives.
hint: Protection before spending, and spending before everyday work.
items: register a second factor for the identity that owns the tenant
create a monthly budget with alerts
keep the spending limit if the offer has one
create an everyday identity with a role on one resource group
trap: The everyday identity comes last because it is lesson 6 and lesson 9; the budget comes before anything that can cost money.

prompt: Which three things come into existence when somebody signs up for Azure?
hint: Only one of them is called an account.

choices.text: A resource group, a virtual network and a storage account
choices.why: None of those is created for you. A new subscription is empty.

choices.text: A management group, a subscription and a budget
choices.why: No budget exists until somebody makes one, which is why making one is step two.

choices.text: A tenant, a subscription and an all-powerful first identity
choices.why: Right. Global Administrator of the tenant and Owner of the subscription, before any second factor.

choices.text: A billing account, a credit card and a region
choices.why: A region is not created: Azure's regions exist already, and you choose one for each resource.

prompt: A student on pay-as-you-go sets a budget of USD 5 with an alert at 100%, then leaves a VPN gateway running for a month. What does the budget do?
hint: What is a budget, and what is a spending limit?

choices.text: You get an e-mail, and the charges carry on
choices.why: Right. An alert tells you; stopping the spending is still yours to do.

choices.text: It switches the subscription to a spending limit
choices.why: Pay as you go has no spending limit, and a budget cannot create one.

choices.text: It deallocates the gateway when the cost reaches USD 5
choices.why: A budget acts on nothing by itself. It notifies.

choices.text: Nothing, since budgets apply only to free accounts
choices.why: Budgets work on any subscription. It is the spending limit that belongs to credit offers.

prompt: Which string does a command accept as the location of a resource in São Paulo?
hint: The portal shows one name and commands take another.

choices.text: `brazilsouth`
choices.why: Right. The programmatic name, all lower case and no spaces.

choices.text: `Brazil South`
choices.why: That is the display name, which the portal shows and no command accepts.

choices.text: `brazil`
choices.why: That is a logical region, a grouping. You cannot deploy into it.

choices.text: `sa-east-1`
choices.why: That is another provider's name for São Paulo. Azure does not know it.

prompt: What is `AzureUSGovernment` in the output of `az cloud list`?
hint: How many copies of Azure does Microsoft run?

choices.text: A region inside the global Azure, reserved for public bodies
choices.why: It is not a region of the global Azure. It has regions of its own, and its own sign-in.

choices.text: A subscription offer with a discount for government
choices.why: It is a separate cloud, not a price.

choices.text: A separate Azure, with regions and sign-in of its own
choices.why: Right. An account in the global Azure does not exist there.

choices.text: A management group Microsoft creates in every tenant
choices.why: Management groups live inside a tenant. A sovereign cloud has tenants of its own.

prompt: Match each address from `az cloud show` to what answers there.
hint: One of them is where an identity proves who it is.

pairs.right: the end of a storage account's address

prompt: A load balancer is zone-redundant and one of the region's three zones fails. What happens to the load balancer?
hint: Who spread it across the zones?

choices.text: It fails, since it lived in the zone that went down
choices.why: That describes a zonal resource. A zone-redundant one lives in all of them.

choices.text: Nobody can tell, because zone failures are not documented
choices.why: Every resource's documentation says whether it is zonal, zone-redundant or regional.

choices.text: It moves to the paired region automatically
choices.why: A zone failure is handled inside the region. The pair is about broad outages and replication.

choices.text: It keeps working, with less capacity
choices.why: Right. Azure spread it across the zones, so losing one costs capacity, not the resource.

prompt: The shop's production subscription runs its database in zone 1. A tester puts a machine in zone 1 of the staging subscription to measure latency "from the same zone". What is wrong with the test?
hint: Who decides what zone 1 means?

choices.text: Nothing: zone 1 is the same datacentre for every subscription
choices.why: Each subscription maps its logical zones on its own, precisely so that everybody's zone 1 is not one building.

choices.text: Each subscription maps its zone 1 on its own
choices.why: Right. Compare the two subscriptions' `availabilityZoneMappings` before trusting the label.

choices.text: Machines in different subscriptions can never talk to each other
choices.why: They can, through the network. The problem is which building each one is in.

choices.text: Staging subscriptions are placed in a different region
choices.why: A subscription is not placed in a region at all; each resource is, and both are in `brazilsouth`.

prompt: Which region is `brazilsouth` paired with?
hint: It is outside Brazil.

choices.text: `brazilsoutheast`
choices.why: Brazil Southeast's pair is Brazil South, but the arrow runs only that way.

choices.text: `northcentralus`
choices.why: That is South Central US's pair, one step further along.

choices.text: `southcentralus`
choices.why: Right. In Texas, and South Central US is paired with somebody else.

choices.text: None: Brazilian regions have no pair
choices.why: Both Brazilian regions have one. It is the newer regions elsewhere that may not.

prompt: A Brazilian clinic must keep patient files in Brazil, and stores them in `brazilsouth` with geo-redundant replication. What has it done?
hint: Where does the second copy go, and who chose it?

choices.text: Kept two copies in São Paulo, in two zones
choices.why: That is zone-redundant replication. Geo-redundant copies to the paired region.

choices.text: Nothing different, since storage never leaves its region
choices.why: Geo-redundant storage exists precisely to leave the region.

choices.text: Kept a copy in Rio de Janeiro, the pair of São Paulo
choices.why: Rio's pair is São Paulo, not the other way round. Replicating to Rio is something the clinic has to arrange itself.

choices.text: Sent a second copy of every file to Texas
choices.why: Right. The pair decides where geo-redundant data goes, and `brazilsouth`'s pair is `southcentralus`.

prompt: Which of these does a region's pair do for you without being asked? Choose all that apply.
hint: Three things are listed at the top of the section.

choices.text: Receives platform updates at a different time from its partner
choices.why: Right. A faulty update reaches one of the two first.

choices.text: Fails your virtual machines over when your region goes down
choices.why: Nothing moves your machines for you. Recovery to another region is a design you build.

choices.text: Holds the second copy of geo-redundant storage
choices.why: Right, and you do not choose where that is.

choices.text: Puts one of the two first in the queue during a broad outage
choices.why: Right. Recovery is prioritised across the pair.

choices.text: Makes data between the two regions free to transfer
choices.why: Data between regions is billed per gigabyte, paired or not.

prompt: In the price program, why does the loop follow `NextPageLink` until it is absent?
hint: How many prices fit in one answer?

choices.text: Because each page is a different currency
choices.why: The currency is set by the request, not by the page.

choices.text: Because one page holds at most a thousand prices
choices.why: Right. Stopping at the first page would silently drop the rest.

choices.text: Because the API requires one request per meter
choices.why: A page holds many meters, up to a thousand.

choices.text: Because the first page holds only expired prices
choices.why: Pages are not sorted by date. They are just the list, cut into pieces.

prompt: Beside any price you repeat, write the date from the field `___`, when that price took effect.
hint: It ends in `Date`.
